questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Saudi Arabia about 2,250,000 square kilometres; Iran about 1,648,195 square kilometres; Turkey about 783,562 square kilometres; Afghanistan about 652,230 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which continent is Saudi Arabia in?

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Saudi Arabia on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Saudi Arabia on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Saudi Arabia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Religion” part of the Saudi Arabia article.

questions.proof: Other big cities are Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Riyadh?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Saudi Arabia is Riyadh.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Saudi Arabia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Saudi Arabia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Saudi Arabia article.

questions.proof: Saudi Arabia is bordered by Jordan and Iraq to the north, Kuwait to the northeast, Qatar, Bahrain, and the United Arab Emirates to the east, Oman to the southeast, and Yemen to the south.
